knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says the owner buys the result and the certainty of getting it, and that rates and tools are inputs. The groomer's clippers, brand and years of experience are not what is bought.
The lesson says a guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford, and that a fix-first promise must be one you can keep. An open-ended or impossible guarantee does not meet this.
The lesson says a measurable claim, such as fewer skin problems after a clip, should not be made unless the result has been measured. Endorsements and discounts do not substantiate it.
